name: Serial Position Effect
description: Items at the beginning and end of a list/sequence are remembered better than items in the middle.
design_relevance_note: Directly informs ordering of navigation items, pricing tiers, and onboarding steps.
prevalence_note: Well known in menu-design and list-ordering discussions (primacy/recency), a standard but not universally foundational reference point.

findings.description: Items presented first (primacy) and last (recency) in a sequence are recalled more accurately than items presented in the middle of the sequence.
findings.source_title: An endogenous distributed model of ordering in serial recall

applications.title: Uber Eats placing an upsell item at the first or last position in a scrollable list
applications.description: Uber Eats' upsell recommendations (e.g. a Crispy Spring Rolls add-on) are positioned at the first or last spot in a scrollable list rather than the middle -- the source suggests this placement isn't incidental, since users naturally give more attention to list-edge positions, especially when browsing under time pressure.
applications.ethical_note: Using attention geometry to place an upsell isn't deceptive on its own -- the item and its price are genuinely what's shown -- but it is a deliberate attempt to increase the odds of an impulse add-on being noticed and selected, which is a real, if mild, influence on the user's purchase decision rather than neutral information design.
